summary: Ran the molecular tests for M1-S04 (tier2-webhook, apex-builder, status built at invocation) after the 2026-09-12 rebuild. Always-on xml: 4/4 .cls-meta.xml parse, all apiVersion 67.0. Always-on manifest: skipped-not-applicable under the Apex exception, naming build-level manifest step M1-S05 (no package.xml exists or is declared for this step). Three declared checkers ran verbatim from the build directory and all exited 0 with zero findings: check_apex_scheduled_jobs.py, check_apex_queueable_patterns.py, check_error_handling_framework.py. check-outputs confirmed all six declared outputs present, non-empty and parseable. One manual test is deferred to the M1 gate, checked against the Given/When/Then observable-outcome bar and found tickable. Step moved built -> tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly (Step 7 HIGH row). No checker was missing, no command was refused, and check-outputs reported ok with nothing missing/empty/malformed.

process_observations.observation: All three declared checkers and the always-on xml check ran clean with zero ERROR/WARN/ADVISORY findings, and deploy-order.md section 8 independently documents the identical exit-0 results plus a brace/paren/bracket balance check this agent re-derived and confirmed.

The step's rebuild trail is fully reconstructable from plan.json amendments[0] plus deploy-order.md section 0, so this test run could confirm the artefacts on disk match the amended inputs (include_logger false, alert_recipients roster) rather than the round-1 P0'd version.

deploy-order.md section 4 records five still-open UNVERIFIED/unbound items on this step's own admission: PermissionSetAssignment read access for resolveRecipients() is granted by nothing this build ships, WITH USER_MODE on an aggregate COUNT() stays unverified against any cited skill, Case record visibility for the third query depends on an unstated OWD, the recipient-gap row counts toward the job's own alert thresholds (a self-inflicted alert loop after ~4 hours with no active assignee), and there is no duplicate-alert suppression across up to 24 hourly repeats. None of these are checker-visible; a green checker run does not mean these are closed.

No org test has run or can run in this design-only build: coverage on Tier2ChannelHealthQueueable is deploy-order.md's own estimate from reading the bodies (~80-95%), not a measured Apex-test number, and no offline compile check exists for Apex in the sf CLI.

plan.json steps[M1-S04].inputs carries two disagreeing keys for the same concept: the older recipients ("Support Engineering", a distribution list) and the 2026-09-12 alert_recipients (active Tier2_Webhook_Admin assignees, which the rebuilt code actually implements). deploy-order.md section 0 already flags this as a stale sibling needing a prose-only amendment. Recorded verbatim per this run's instruction; not resolved here, since amend-step is refused once a step has left pending and resolving it is a plan edit, not a test-runner action.

The step's own acceptance_tests[] manifest-test description says the build-level manifest step M1-S05 carries "the three ApexClass members" from this step, but the rebuilt artefacts on disk ship four (Schedulable, Queueable, Test, TestDataFactory) -- the description predates the TestDataFactory template-provenance addition. Does not change the manifest classification (still skipped-not-applicable, still naming M1-S05), but M1-S05's own test run should expect four members from this step, not three.

The step's manual acceptance test is not written in literal Given/When/Then clauses, but it names three concrete observable outcomes (the CRON literal's value, the two Q24 threshold values, the sender address plus a named person's org-verification confirmation). Judged tickable rather than unusable, but a human reviewer could reasonably want it reformatted into strict Given/When/Then before the M1 gate.
Step is now tested; build-doc-keeper is the next stage of the loop for this step.
